thread.title: FBI-Kansas City and KCPD receive award for efforts against youth opioid overdoses
thread.title_full: FBI-Kansas City and KCPD receive award for efforts against youth opioid overdoses

author: KC Reporter
title: FBI-Kansas City and KCPD receive award for efforts against youth opioid overdoses
text:
The Federal Bureau of Investigation-Kansas City Transnational Organized Crime Squad and the Kansas City Police Department Drug Investigation Squad received the 2026 Crystal Kipper & Ali Kemp Memorial Award, presented by United States Attorney R. Matthew Price for the Western District of Missouri on May 27.
The annual award honors the memory of Crystal Kipper and Ali Kemp, both fatal victims of violent crimes. The ceremony took place in the Western District, where Price recognized a task force led by FBI Special Agent Ellen Judy, Supervisory Special Agent Joseph Michael, retired Detective Cory Horalek, and Sergeant Aaron Benson. The team coordinates federal, state, and local agencies to address fentanyl overdose deaths in greater Kansas City.
Other law enforcement partners include the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives; Internal Revenue Service-Criminal Investigations; U.S. Border Patrol; Missouri State Highway Patrol; Jackson County Drug Task Force; Platte County Sheriff’s Office; Clay County Sheriff’s Office; among others. The group investigated a drug trafficking organization that sold counterfeit oxycodone pills containing fentanyl via social media. Their actions resulted in the death of a 17-year-old from Olathe, Kansas.
The investigation led to charges against 13 defendants with successful prosecutions and further investigations resulting in charges against at least 14 more individuals. Authorities seized large quantities of drugs valued at over $4 million as well as firearms and cash during their work. The task force’s efforts contributed to a decrease in overdose deaths within the district.
Price presented the award alongside Anna Kipper Rea (mother of Crystal Kipper) and Jill and Bob Leiker from the Ali Kemp Educational Foundation. This marks the 22nd year for this recognition commemorating two young women who were murdered—Crystal Kipper at age 18 near Platte City in February 1997 after running out of gas on Interstate 29, and Ali Kemp at age 19 while working at a Leawood swimming pool in June 2002.
The Crystal Kipper & Ali Kemp Memorial Award is given annually by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for outstanding contributions toward preventing violent crime or child exploitation, according to the official website . The office supports community outreach programs targeting violent crime and drug trafficking across its jurisdiction from Iowa to Arkansas borders through collaboration with multiple law enforcement partners.
